title: Which Payments are Struck Against the Arrears Figure
content:
Which of the payments standing on the premium account of one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders are struck against the arrears figure follows from the rider's standing.

## The rule

**Where the rider stands at active and the rider record carries no day it ended**, only the payments posted within the days of grace that govern are struck.

**Where the rider stands in its waiting period**, only the payments posted from the day benefits became payable are struck.

**Otherwise**, every payment posted to the rider premium account is struck.

## Condition and payments struck

| The rider's standing | The payments struck |
|---|---|
| Active, the record carrying no day it ended | Those posted within the days of grace that govern |
| In its waiting period | Those posted from the day benefits became payable |
| Any other standing | Every payment on the account |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

A rider premium account carries payments of 46.90 USD, 46.90 USD and 20.00 USD, posted in three successive calendar months up to and including the month of handling, the days of grace that govern giving a span of 2 whole months.

- **Active, with no day it ended:** the two posted within the span are struck, 66.90 USD.
- **In its waiting period, benefits having become payable at the start of the second of those months:** the two posted from that day are struck, 66.90 USD.
- **Suspended for unpaid premium, or ended:** all three are struck, 113.80 USD.

## Note

The first case turns on two things together — the rider standing at active, and the record carrying no day it ended. A rider standing at active whose record carries a day it ended falls to the third case, where every payment on the account is struck.
